lead: there is a list of what you are responsible for, and you agreed to two items on it. the rest went on without a conversation, at the point where people worked out that you had somewhere to put them.
sun: two commitments carried at full weight do not read as two commitments. from outside they read as one that has not been settled, and an unsettled person is assumed to have slack in the week. so the fork is the credential: everybody who has left something with you ran the same quick arithmetic and got the same answer, that you are not fully spoken for. nobody has ever had to show their working.
moon: a week after it lands, the thing has stopped being something anybody did and become a fact about you that predates whoever mentions it — the accounts, the aunt's affairs, the keys to a building you have no interest in. nothing was ever accepted out loud, and a thing that was never accepted has no procedure for being handed back.
pull: the gap between your two directions is the only part of your life anybody has ever left anything in. nobody asked, and by now nobody remembers that there was anything to ask.
tension: the year the accounts went in late, two of the people who put them on you were the ones who noticed, and both were fair about it, and both filed it. easy-going is what gets said, warmly, by people who have watched you take on things nobody sane would take on and have never watched anybody ask. the two you chose get whatever hours are left, and when one of those slips it slips against the same character.
cost: a thing left with you is genuinely held. the estate ran four years without a query, the animal lived, the paperwork was in order, and whoever put it there never had to think about it. the two directions you actually chose have no such protection. both run on the hours nobody else has claimed, and both have been described, kindly, as what you do instead of getting on.

lead: your sister says she is fine about the sale. that she is fine about the sale is true, and the other thing is true, and neither reading gets demoted. you answer both. she has heard one answer.
sun: most people who hear two versions of a sentence keep one and treat the other as manners, which is what makes the hearing usable. no ranking arrives here. the spoken account is entire and the unspoken one is entire, both get acted on, and the acting takes two shapes — a reply, which lands inside the conversation, and four months of arrangements, which land where nobody can attach them to anything.
moon: the second account arrives with the listening, invited or not, and it arrives with its work already attached — by the time you register it, the arrangements are half made. the spoken half is the only half that can be thanked, since thanking you for the other one would mean saying out loud the sentence they took care not to say.
pull: you were told one thing and you heard two, and you have been answering the second one for years in a currency nobody in the room can name.
tension: people come away from you feeling heard and unable to report what you said, which is warm for a while and then becomes a complaint. hard to get a straight answer out of. the straight answer went to the sentence they spoke; the rest of you went to the sentence they did not, and offering that as an account means telling somebody what you heard them nearly say. the ones who would recognise it are the ones who would mind.
cost: somebody can get the difficult part handled without ever having admitted it out loud, and that has been the arrangement with the same four or five people for twenty years — nobody has to be brave with you. it is unwitnessed by construction. everything you are owed sits inside a version of events that the person owing it has never agreed took place.

lead: nobody has been told there are two calendars. what reaches people is a pattern, heavy then light then heavy, and they have arranged fifteen years against it and given it a name that is a fact about your character.
sun: the pattern has a cause and the cause is arithmetic. two commitments, each with its own heavy season, and the seasons do not consult each other, so what any one group receives is the sum. neither half is being fitted around the other — both get the weeks they need when they need them — and the sum is what goes out into the world as a temperament.
moon: a rate other people hold without deciding to does not need to be regular to be held. it needs to be reliable, and yours is: the same composite, year after year. so a beat with no single source is being kept by two sets of people who did not choose it, and the twice-a-year fortnight when both heavy seasons land at once arrives to them as the whole arrangement failing.
pull: the beat everybody sets their week by is the sum of two calendars, and the one thing that would explain your good weeks and your bad ones is that there are two.
tension: you are accused of being a lot, and the accusation is accurate. a beat has to keep coming out to exist, so there is more of you around than a room asks for — the messages, the calls, the thing sent on a saturday. one person has asked why any of it needs announcing. the announcing is what keeps two sets of people running to the same time, and each set sees only its own half of the reason.
cost: twenty years, two sets of people, and neither has had to wonder where you went. the beat is what buys that and the beat is also what spends the week. every year has the same number of transmitting weeks in it as the last one, and no year has ever contained a run at anything, because a run at anything requires going off the air.

lead: come and stay is a sentence you have said and meant, in both halves of your life, to people who will never meet. there is one spare room, and neither promise was ever the smaller one.
sun: the offer costs the same to make out of either half, and you have made it out of both. what neither person is told, because it does not present itself to you as information, is that the week they are arriving into already has two full claims on it. a place can be given whole. the hours cannot, and nothing in you has ever ranked which of the two a tuesday belongs to.
moon: the making of room here is a decided thing that goes into words, which is why it holds. somebody told at thirty does not have to ask again at fifty. so two people hold the same promise, in the same words, over the same eleven square feet, and both of them are correct, and neither was ever the practice run for the other.
pull: two people have been told the same true thing about your door, years apart, and both are right. what nobody has been given is the sentence that puts one of them first.
tension: guests leave having been housed properly and having seen you for about half the hours they came for, and the half is what gets remembered. a week in your spare room comes with a host who goes into the other thing on the tuesday. nobody has ever complained about the bed. what gets said afterwards is that you were hard to get hold of in your own house, which sounds exactly like somebody who did not want the company.
cost: the promise holds its full size in two people, and neither was told to wait; somebody at their worst can arrive on no notice and find the sentence exactly where they left it. what has not happened to either is being the only one in the house. no guest has ever arrived and found the week clear. the place was real every time and it was never anybody's alone.
